solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Make sure gullible person’s collecting right fabric (10)

indicatorNotes.collecting: the sucker gathers R up, so R sits inside SEE+SUCKER

blocks.note: to see that something happens is to make sure of it
a sucker is someone easily fooled

annotation.surface: A con artist making certain a mark picks up the correct cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: The collected letter lands exactly at the join of the two words, which is why it can read as a plain run of three parts.
annotation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a thin puckered cotton fabric, often striped.

entries.clue: Reasonable except when noun plays part of verb (4)

indicatorNotes.plays part of: N takes over V's role, like an actor playing a part

blocks.note: save = except, as in all save one
V = verb; N replaces it in SAVE

annotation.surface: A grammar rule: fine, except where a noun does a verb's job.
annotation.walkthrough: "Except when" looks like part of the grammar rule, but "except" is SAVE and "when" just links it to the swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sane decision is a reasonable one, sound in judgement.

entries.clue: Retired engineers excluded from training duties (7)

indicatorNotes.excluded from: taken out of the next word

blocks.note: RE (Royal Engineers) backwards; take it out of EXERCISES

annotation.surface: Former army engineers left off the drill rota.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps. Remove ER from EXERCISES.
annotation.definitionFit: Excises are duties, taxes on goods made or sold at home.

entries.clue: Short nurse taking home English man left in holy place (7,6)

indicatorNotes.Short: a word cut short has lost its end, so SISTER drops its final R
indicatorNotes.taking: SISTE takes the next pieces inside it

blocks.note: SISTER (a senior nurse) without its last letter
L = left, added at the end

annotation.surface: A nurse on a short shift taking an Englishman home, with a man left behind in church.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a sister is a senior nurse. The nurse takes in three pieces, not just home, and left stays outside at the very end.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Vatican's papal chapel is one holy place, famous for Michelangelo's ceiling.

entries.clue: Cold fish crossing large marsh recalled leggy six-footer (5,3)

indicatorNotes.crossing: the fish lies across, so around, the marsh

blocks.note: a ray is a flat fish

annotation.surface: A chilly fish swimming across a big swamp, remembered as a long-legged creature.
annotation.walkthrough: "Six-footer" suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet. A crane fly is a daddy-long-legs.
annotation.definitionFit: A crane fly is an insect, so six-legged, with notably long legs.

entries.clue: Cycling centre generates electrical connection (5)

indicatorNotes.Cycling: the first letter goes round to the back

blocks.note: the heart of something is its centre; its H then cycles to the back

annotation.surface: A power plant at a cycle hub making electricity.
annotation.walkthrough: British usage: what Americans call a ground wire is an earth in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in British wiring the safety connection to the ground takes the planet's own name.

entries.clue: Macho gear periodically sent west for commander (4)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals: every other letter
indicatorNotes.sent west: in an across clue, going west is going right to left

blocks.note: every other letter, starting from the second: mAcHo GeAr

annotation.surface: Tough-guy kit being shipped out for an officer.
annotation.walkthrough: An agha is an Ottoman title for a chief; it turns up in crosswords far more than in life.
annotation.definitionFit: An agha was a military commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire.

entries.clue: Slender holy object inscribed with C and E (7)

indicatorNotes.inscribed with: C is written into the grail

blocks.note: E, as printed, goes on the end

annotation.surface: A thin sacred relic engraved with a couple of letters.
annotation.walkthrough: Only C goes inside; E follows at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly literary or scientific: anthropologists call slender-boned early humans by this word, related to graceful.

entries.clue: Quite good anaesthetic agent bolstering singer (10)

indicatorNotes.bolstering: in a down clue, what supports another word sits under it

annotation.surface: A decent anaesthetic propping up a singer.
annotation.walkthrough: "Quite good" reads as mild praise; "quite" alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Altogether means quite, entirely: "not altogether sure".

entries.clue: American coin is fluid capital (7)

indicatorNotes.fluid: the letters are free to flow into a new order

annotation.surface: A remark about the dollar as a liquid asset: American money as fluid capital.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fluid capital" reads as one money phrase; it splits into the anagram indicator and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Nicosia is one capital city among many, that of Cyprus.

entries.clue: Perform again on time after Rod returned (2-5)

indicatorNotes.after: T comes after the rod in the answer

blocks.note: RE = on, concerning, as in a memo
a cane is a rod; backwards it is ENAC

annotation.surface: A stage direction for a performer called Rod, back and on cue.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rod" looks like a name, capital R and all, but it is an ordinary rod: a cane.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym built from its parts: the prefix re- means again, and to enact a scene is to perform it.

entries.clue: Northern town magazine’s covering of macabre shop (9,4)

indicatorNotes.covering of: the letters on the outside of the word

blocks.note: Elle is a fashion magazine, with its 's
to shop someone is to report them to the police

annotation.surface: A magazine's feature on a grisly shop somewhere in the North.
annotation.walkthrough: Ellesmere Port is a town in Cheshire, in north-west England. To shop someone is British slang for informing on them.
annotation.definitionFit: Ellesmere Port is a port town in north-west England.

entries.clue: Scary Carol circling Charlie on long slope (5-8)

indicatorNotes.circling: to circle something is to go all the way round it, so the carol's letters surround the rest
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, C comes on after PINE

blocks.note: to carol is to sing; it wraps round the middle
to long for is to pine for
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A woman named Carol skiing round a friend on a steep run, which sounds frightening.
annotation.walkthrough: "Carol" looks like a name, but it is the verb: to sing.
annotation.definitionFit: Spine-chilling means frightening enough to send a shiver down the back.

entries.clue: Advice Bishop Lee put out is taken in easily? (10)

indicatorNotes.put out: disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Asking whether a man called Lee is gullible once a bishop's counsel upsets him.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that "taken in easily" is a loose paraphrase of deceivable.
annotation.definitionFit: Deceivable means able to be deceived, taken in.

entries.clue: Wind last of Omega watches at the bazaar in city (8)

indicatorNotes.last of: take the final letter of each of the following words
indicatorNotes.in: the letters go inside the city

blocks.note: ELY, the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, opened up to take the rest
last letters: omegA watcheS aT thE bazaaR

annotation.surface: Browsing Omega watches on a market stall somewhere in town.
annotation.walkthrough: "Last of" is singular but covers every word from Omega to bazaar; Omega looks like the brand of watch, but only its A counts.
annotation.definitionFit: Winds are named for the direction they come from, and one from the east is called by the noun formed from that direction.

entries.clue: Mounting agreement by the sound of it (6)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: judge the word by how it is said, not spelt

blocks.note: assent is formal agreement; say it and spell it a different way

annotation.surface: Growing agreement, as far as one can hear.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mounting" looks like an adjective (growing agreement) but here it is a noun: the act of going up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mounting a hill and making a climb up it both describe going up.

entries.clue: First son observed husband’s drilling power tool (8)

indicatorNotes.drilling: H bores its way into CAIN

blocks.note: Cain, first son of Adam and Eve
H = husband, from genealogy and marriage records

annotation.surface: A son watching his father operate a drill.
annotation.walkthrough: "First son" is not an S; it is Cain, Genesis's firstborn.
annotation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a powered saw with teeth on a moving chain.

entries.clue: Manage spinning empty half-truths for ages (6)

indicatorNotes.spinning: turned round, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.empty: with the inside removed, only the outer letters stay

blocks.note: to cope is to manage; backwards it is EPOC

annotation.surface: A spin doctor turning out hollow half-truths for years on end.
annotation.walkthrough: "Manage spinning" suggests spin doctors, but spinning simply turns COPE round.
annotation.definitionFit: Epochs are long periods of time, ages.

entries.clue: Where you may get crabs and more shelled fish on delta (7)

indicatorNotes.shelled: its shell, the outer letters, removed
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, placed on top of D

blocks.note: char is a fish of the trout family
Delta is D in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A seafood guide: crabs, plus other shellfish served on a river delta.
annotation.walkthrough: The crabs are crab apples, not crustaceans; the seafood surface hides the fruit tree.
annotation.definitionFit: Crab apples grow on trees, so an orchard is where you may pick crabs.

entries.clue: Tie small hearts to nameless Xmas card (8)

indicatorNotes.nameless: without N, the abbreviation for name

blocks.note: an ace is a playing card

annotation.surface: Tying little hearts onto an unsigned Christmas card.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tie" looks like a verb in the surface but is the noun: a thing that ties a shoe.
annotation.definitionFit: A shoelace is a lace used to tie a shoe, so a tie.

entries.clue: Presenter’s prompt US vehicle at head of line reported (7)

indicatorNotes.at head of: in a down clue, placed above the next piece
indicatorNotes.reported: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a queue is a line of people; CUE sounds the same

annotation.surface: A TV host's cue about an American car leading a queue.
annotation.walkthrough: Autocue is the British trade name for a teleprompter.
annotation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen that feeds a presenter lines: a prompt.

entries.clue: Fault occupant entertaining Penny in deputy’s office (4,9)

annotation.definitionNote: a phrase describing the person rather than a noun: the vice president is the one in the deputy's post

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so P goes inside

blocks.note: a vice is a moral fault

annotation.surface: A tenant with a flaw having a woman called Penny round at the deputy's office.
annotation.walkthrough: P goes in right after the first letter of RESIDENT; "Penny" looks like a guest's name but is the coin.
annotation.definitionFit: A vice president holds the deputy's office, next below the president.

entries.clue: Blues guys alternately backing key song in service? (5)

indicatorNotes.alternately: taking turns, as the guys in the surface do, so the letters are used every other one
indicatorNotes.backing: in a down clue, supporting from below, so after

annotation.surface: Blues men taking turns backing a singer in a particular key.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the loose definition: an elegy is a lament, as might be sung at a funeral service.
annotation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful song or poem for the dead.

entries.clue: Replacement handle missing essential part, unfortunately (4)

indicatorNotes.missing essential part: losing its essence, its central letter

blocks.note: an alias is a stand-in name, and a handle is a name; its middle I is the essential part that goes

annotation.surface: A spare door handle lacking a vital piece, sadly.
annotation.walkthrough: "Handle" looks like a door handle; it is slang for a name.
annotation.definitionFit: The interjection does the job of the adverb: saying it before bad news is the same as prefacing it with unfortunately.

entries.clue: Some expel liar bleating about dots on pages (7)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the following words is used

annotation.surface: Throwing out a whining liar.
annotation.walkthrough: Read from the B of bleating back to the E of expel.
annotation.definitionFit: Braille is the writing system of raised dots read by touch.

entries.clue: Long-suffering saint painting around edges of cupola (7)

indicatorNotes.around: the painting goes round the next letters
indicatorNotes.edges of: only the first and last letters

blocks.note: an oil is an oil painting

annotation.surface: A patient saint enduring a painting of a dome.
annotation.walkthrough: "Painting" is a noun here, an oil, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Stoical means enduring hardship without complaint, as the long-suffering do.

entries.clue: Twisted reptile losing tail in mythic poems (4)

indicatorNotes.Twisted: turned round so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.losing tail: a word's tail is its end, so the reptile sheds its last letter as a lizard sheds its tail

blocks.note: ADDER (a snake) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A snake that has lost its tail, coiled up in a legend.
annotation.walkthrough: "Losing tail" is apt for a reptile, since lizards shed theirs; here it just drops the R.
annotation.definitionFit: The Edda is a collection of Old Norse mythological poems.

entries.clue: Who’s first seen yeti moving close to tents? (10)

annotation.definition: Who’s first seen yeti moving close to tents?

indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of Who
indicatorNotes.moving: the letters move into a new order
indicatorNotes.close to: the close, or end, of tents: its last letter

annotation.surface: Asking who spotted the yeti prowling near the camp.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: an eyewitness is whoever first sees the yeti near the tents.
annotation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is someone who saw an event with their own eyes.
